articles.title: England appoint Eric Simons to Stephen Fleming's Test coaching team
articles.summary: England are set to add the first name to Stephen Fleming’s backroom team, with Eric Simons joining as Test bowling coach.
articles.body:
England are set to add the first name to Stephen Fleming's backroom team, with Eric Simons joining as Test bowling coach.

Former South Africa head coach Simons is a long-time ally of Fleming, having worked alongside him in the Indian Premier League (IPL) with Chennai Super Kings.

Simons' new role will be confirmed on Monday, when England announce the latest round of central contracts.

New Zealander Fleming is assembling a backroom team for his first series in charge, against South Africa in December.

The shake-up in the staff comes as England once again split head-coaching responsibilities across formats. Fleming is in charge of the Test side and Brendon McCullum leads the white-ball teams.

When McCullum was Test coach, England used a number of fast-bowling consultants, including James Anderson, David Saker and Tim Southee.

Saker will be part of the England staff for the one-day tri-series in Pakistan this month, alongside long-term McCullum assistant Jeetan Patel, Mike Yardy and Carl Hopkinson.

Southee and fielding coach Sarah Taylor, who have been with England throughout the home summer, might rejoin the team later in the winter.

Kevin Pietersen has been appointed as a batting consultant to the white-ball teams in the run-up to the 50-over World Cup in southern Africa.

Former England batter Pietersen will not be on the tour of Pakistan, but is due to join the squad for the white-ball tour of Australia and then in South Africa for the three one-day internationals in the country of his birth in January.

Marcus Trescothick took interim charge of the Test team for the series against Pakistan. His future in the England set-up has been the subject of speculation and is yet to be confirmed.

Simons, 64, played 23 one-day internationals for South Africa in 1994 and 1995.

He also worked with Fleming at the Joburg Super Kings in the SA20 and the Texas Super Kings in Major League Cricket.

Simons had two years in charge of the South Africa team between 2002 and 2004 and a spell as India's bowling coach.

articles.title: ‘Virat was a bit bitter’: Former India cricketer drops big verdict on Kohli's Test retirement
articles.summary: Virat Kohli's retirement from Test cricket may have come as a surprise to many, but former India cricketer Wasim Jaffer believes the star batter was
articles.body: Virat Kohli's retirement from Test cricket may have come as a surprise to many, but former India cricketer Wasim Jaffer believes the star batter was unhappy with how his exit was handled. Jaffer feels Kohli could have continued playing the longest format and said the circumstances surrounding his retirement could have been managed better.“Yes, absolutely. I mean, it seemed like Virat was a bit bitter about how things were handled,” Jaffer said on his YouTube channel, as quoted by India Today.“A player like Virat, he draws crowds to the stadium; he has such a massive following. He definitely could have played more Test cricket. Until we hear directly from Virat what the actual situation was, we won't know for sure.”Kohli's retirement came after months of uncertainty over his future in Test cricket. The former India captain had been keen to continue playing the format and tour England. He had also represented Delhi in a Ranji Trophy match in January 2025, underlining his commitment to red-ball cricket.However, the situation reportedly changed in April. Kohli was reportedly left disillusioned by the developments and later informed the selectors that he did not want to be part of the England tour. Attempts by people close to him and some BCCI officials to convince him to reconsider did not succeed.Jaffer pointed to Kohli's preparations for the England tour as a reason to question how the situation had been handled.“But I mean, he was preparing; he was gearing up for the England tour. So, all those things could have been handled better. As I said, regarding certain individuals, things could have been managed better,” Jaffer said.Kohli announced his retirement from Test cricket on May 12, 2025, ending a 14-year career in the format. articles.title: 'West Indies, you can never take them lightly': Shreyas Iyer after India take 2-1 lead
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India captain Shreyas Iyer praised his bowlers for their confident approach and clear plans after the team defeated the West Indies by 14 runs
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India captain Shreyas Iyer praised his bowlers for their confident approach and clear plans after the team defeated the West Indies by 14 runs in the third T20I at Holkar Stadium on Sunday. The victory gave India a 2-1 lead in the five-match series.India successfully defended a target of 224, restricting the West Indies to 209/7. Arshdeep Singh took three wickets, while Naman Dhir picked up two scalps to help India stop the visitors from completing another successful chase.Iyer impressed with bowlers' approachIyer said the bowlers knew what they wanted to do and backed themselves to execute their plans under pressure."It was wonderful because the bowlers were pretty confident with what they wanted to execute. The clarity was much more visible. They were decisive in their execution and when I was passing the ball to them, each and every bowler was up for the challenge and that's what you want," Iyer said during the post-match presentation.Arshdeep played a key role in the defence, finishing with figures of 3/44. He dismissed in-form opener Shai Hope early and later removed Keemo Paul and Sherfane Rutherford in the 18th over to put India firmly in control.Dhir also made an important contribution with two wickets, including the dismissal of Kamil Pooran, who had threatened to turn the game around with an aggressive innings.Iyer praises Abhishek and KishanIndia's strong start with the bat came from Abhishek Sharma and Ishan Kishan. Abhishek smashed 69 off 30 balls, while Kishan scored 37 off just 18 deliveries.Iyer praised both batters for giving India momentum at the top of the order. He also highlighted Prince Yadav's contribution towards the end of the innings."Honestly, that was a phenomenal start. Abhishek doing what he does in the powerplay and Kishan coming in. He's been great in the last few months. Even Prince (Yadav) playing the cameo in the end, those were crucial runs."West Indies, you can never take them lightly. So, we had to make sure we never got complacent. These are high-scoring grounds but it's important to stick to our process and follow our routines and make sure we stay offensive," Iyer said.Hetmyer and Pooran threaten India's defenceThe West Indies began their chase with an early setback when Arshdeep bowled Shai Hope for one. However, Shimron Hetmyer counterattacked and made the most of a dropped catch by Abhishek Sharma at short third man.Hetmyer struck boundaries against the Indian bowlers and scored 43 before being bowled by a slower delivery from Dhir.Rovman Powell fell for five after attempting a big shot against Axar Patel. Pooran then attacked Dhir, hitting three sixes in an attempt to bring the West Indies back into the contest.However, Dhir dismissed Pooran for 42 when the batter attempted another pick-up shot but failed to get enough elevation.Arshdeep seals India's victorySherfane Rutherford and Quention Sampson tried to rebuild the innings with some aggressive batting. Sampson, however, was caught at long-off off Nitish Kumar Reddy.Arshdeep then struck twice in four balls during the 18th over, dismissing Keemo Paul and Rutherford to leave the West Indies with too much to do.Shamar Springer provided some late excitement with an unbeaten 35 off just 11 balls, but his effort was not enough to take the visitors over the line. The West Indies finished on 209/7, falling 14 runs short.The result also marked the first victory for a team batting first in the white-ball series so far. India had looked set for a bigger total after Abhishek's explosive innings, but a series of soft dismissals in the second half of their innings had given the West Indies hope.India's bowlers made sure that the late batting collapse did not cost the team the match, helping the hosts move ahead in the T20I series.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Let them do whatever': Mohammed Shami breaks silence on continued India snubs
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Mohammed Shami has responded to questions about his fitness and bowling rhythm, saying he is focused on playing cricket rather than paying
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Mohammed Shami has responded to questions about his fitness and bowling rhythm, saying he is focused on playing cricket rather than paying attention to outside comments.The Bengal fast bowler made the remarks after taking four wickets against Delhi in Bengal's opening match of the 2026-27 Ranji Trophy season in Kalyani on Sunday. His figures of 4/30 helped Bengal bowl Delhi out for 240 on the first day.The 36-year-old has been out of favour with the national selectors, but he said he would continue playing wherever he gets an opportunity instead of worrying about his return to the Indian team.'It doesn't bother me'Shami said people were free to comment on his fitness and performances, but he would continue to focus on his game."People perhaps enjoy looking and passing comments more. They say the rhythm isn't there, that he doesn't look fit, or whatever else. It doesn't bother me. I'm on the ground, I'm playing, and I'm playing wherever I'm given a chance. The rest is your job," Shami said during a press conference.The fast bowler was once again left out of India's squad, this time for the T20I series against New Zealand. The selection also marked the return of Bhuvneshwar Kumar to the national team after a gap of four years.Asked about his own omission, Shami said he no longer wanted to comment on selection decisions and would concentrate on playing cricket."I have stopped making such comments. It makes no difference to me. Now, whoever wants to do whatever, let them. My job is just to play," he added.Shami hails Bhuvneshwar's returnShami also supported the decision to bring Bhuvneshwar back into India's T20I squad. He said the experienced pacer's return should encourage other players to keep working hard and believing in their abilities.The Bengal pacer stressed that talented players who continue to perform should not be kept out of the team for long periods."A person should keep going on hope alone," Shami said."Look at the skill he has. It's not as if he hasn't been talking to anyone or anything like that. That doesn't mean you should keep a talent out for a long time. I'm happy for him because this has come after such a long time. He has also delivered performances consistently in the IPL. If someone is working hard, showing their skill and has the potential, why shouldn't they be playing? Everyone deserves a chance to perform."Shami's comments came as he continued to make his case through performances in domestic cricket. He said he remained motivated to play for as long as he wanted to continue his career.Four wickets put Bengal in controlShami backed up his words with a strong performance against Delhi in the Ranji Trophy opener.After Bengal elected to bowl, their pace attack made good use of the movement available on the pitch. Shami led the effort with four wickets for 30 runs, while Akash Deep took two wickets for 74 runs and Mukesh Kumar claimed one for 43.Off-spinner Amir Ghani also played an important role, taking three wickets for 45 runs.Shami dismissed Yash Dhull, Ayush Doseja, Hrithik Shokeen and Divij Mehra. Shokeen was Delhi's top scorer, making 56 off 98 balls, before Shami removed him.Delhi were eventually bowled out for 240 in 77.3 overs, giving Bengal a strong start to their campaign.With another impressive domestic performance, Shami showed that he remains focused on proving himself on the field rather than responding to questions about his fitness or selection.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: After 15 years, Team India's tailender achieves rare T20I feat: Prince Yadav joins Sreesanth, Ashwin
articles.summary: Prince Yadav has joined S Sreesanth and Ravichandran Ashwin on a rare list of Indian batters after hitting three fours against the West Indies in the
articles.body: Prince Yadav has joined S Sreesanth and Ravichandran Ashwin on a rare list of Indian batters after hitting three fours against the West Indies in the third T20I in Indore on Sunday. He became only the third Indian batter batting at No. 10 or No. 11 to hit at least three boundaries in a T20 International.The feat came after a gap of 15 years, with Ashwin being the last Indian batter to achieve it in 2011. Prince's late contribution also helped India reach 223 before the hosts secured a 14-run victory to take a 2-1 lead in the five-match series.Prince joins Sreesanth and AshwinSreesanth tops the list with four boundaries against New Zealand in Johannesburg in 2007. Ashwin hit three fours against England in Kolkata in 2011, while Prince matched his tally against the West Indies in Indore in 2026.Prince's achievement came 19 years after Sreesanth's effort and 15 years after Ashwin's innings.Most boundaries by an Indian No. 10 or No. 11 in a T20IBoundariesBatterOppositionVenueYear4S SreesanthNew ZealandJohannesburg20073Ravichandran AshwinEnglandKolkata20113Prince YadavWest IndiesIndore2026Three boundaries in the final overPrince came out to bat in the 19th over with India at 202/8. With wickets falling towards the end of the innings, he made the most of his opportunity by hitting three fours off Shamar Joseph.He opened his account with a boundary through deep mid-wicket off a low full toss. Two balls later, he read the delivery well and scooped it over wicketkeeper Shai Hope for another four.Prince then got a thick top edge off a short-of-length delivery, which flew over short third man to give him his third boundary of the over. He also ran a bye during the over as the West Indies players questioned the umpire's decision.His quick scoring helped India add useful runs at a crucial stage and finish with 223.India bowlers seal 14-run winAbhishek Sharma had laid the foundation for India's total with a 30-ball 69, while Ishan Kishan contributed 37 off just 18 deliveries. However, India's progress slowed after a series of wickets in the second half of the innings.The bowlers made sure those late setbacks did not prove costly. Arshdeep Singh picked up three wickets for 44 runs, while Naman Dhir claimed two as the West Indies finished on 209/7.Shamar Springer gave the visitors hope with an unbeaten 35 off just 11 balls, but India held on for a 14-run win.The victory put India 2-1 ahead in the five-match series.The fourth T20I will be played in Hyderabad on Wednesday.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Shikhar Mohan, another boy from Ranchi, who is making himself count
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Shikhar Mohan hails from Doranda, a familiar corner of Ranchi known for its educational institutions, PG accommodations and its much-loved
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Shikhar Mohan hails from Doranda, a familiar corner of Ranchi known for its educational institutions, PG accommodations and its much-loved litti chokha stall, whose popularity extends beyond the city limits.“Wo mandir ke paas wala shop... kaafi famous hai ab (That stall near the temple is pretty famous now),” said Shikhar, referring to Bhola Litti, a popular eating joint that he considers one of the best places for litti chokha.The 21-year-old, who has lived all his life in Doranda, is arguably the hottest cricketing talent in India right now. Former India spinner and current Jharkhand State Cricket Association (JSCA) official Shahbaz Nadeem calls Shikhar Mohan a prodigious talent. "Lambi race ka ghoda hai, alag hi talent hai (He is a long-term prospect with exceptional talent)," Nadeem told TimesofIndia.com.The second season is always more important because the opposition knows more about you. Teams analyse your strengths and weaknesses, so you have to keep improving.The opener has indeed walked the talk. After an excellent debut season in 2025-26, in which he amassed 613 runs at an average of 55.73, including two centuries, he has started the new season in rollicking fashion, smashing 143 in Jharkhand's opening match against Kerala at the Keenan Stadium in Jamshedpur. The southpaw also made some valuable contributions in the Duleep Trophy final for East Zone, scoring 85 and 52 in both innings, followed by a solid 60 on a green top in Srinagar in the Irani Trophy, playing for Rest of India against defending Ranji Trophy champions Jammu and Kashmir."I want to perform as well as I did last season. The second season is always more important because the opposition knows more about you. Teams analyse your strengths and weaknesses, so you have to keep improving," Shikhar Mohan told this website on the eve of their match."More importantly, I want the team to do well. We reached the final last year, and I want us to go one step further. We have won the white-ball tournament (Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy). Now, our plan is to win a red-ball tournament as well. I want to have another good season," he said.Shikhar has already made a great start to the Ranji Trophy season and credits it to the 25-day camp held in Chennai."We had a camp in Chennai for around 25 days before the Duleep Trophy. We trained during the afternoon in the Chennai heat. We also played in the KSCA tournament. Preparation has been on point," he said.During the Duleep Trophy final in Chennai, Ishan bhai helped me understand which shots were appropriate for those conditions. For example, he told me there was no need to play the sweep shot in certain situations. He helped me understand what to play and what to avoid. That guidance made a big difference when I was building my innings.Shikhar admits that he was a bit nervous on the morning of the Duleep Trophy final. Despite training in Chennai for three weeks, it was his first time playing on a red-soil wicket. His state-mate and East Zone skipper Ishan Kishan helped him understand the conditions and guided him during the match. The duo put on 94 runs for the fourth wicket in the first innings and added 126 runs in the second."I spoke to Ishan bhaiya a lot during the last season as well. He would tell me which shots I should play and which ones I should avoid," he said."In the East, we do not get many red-soil wickets. We generally play on black-soil surfaces, so I did not have much experience batting on red soil. During the Duleep Trophy final in Chennai, Ishan bhai helped me understand which shots were appropriate for those conditions. For example, he told me there was no need to play the sweep shot in certain situations. He helped me understand what to play and what to avoid. That guidance made a big difference when I was building my innings," Shikhar added.Shikhar, who was selected for Jharkhand's Under-16 team when he was only 13, has been a prolific run-getter at every age-group level. He enjoyed back-to-back excellent seasons with the Under-23 side in the Col CK Nayudu Trophy. In the 2023-24 season, he scored 623 runs, including two hundreds and three fifties. He continued his run-scoring spree the following season, scoring 887 runs, which helped him earn a call-up to the senior side.Despite his impressive run with the bat, big, headlines-grabbing scores were missing. Shikhar realised that he was experiencing lapses in concentration midway through his innings and received help from current Jharkhand coach Ratan Kumar and former Jharkhand veteran Ishank Jaggi.Before facing a ball, I talk to myself. I remind myself to watch the ball and stay focused. That has helped me a lot. Ishank Jaggi bhai also helped me with this, especially when he was with the Under-19 team. I started concentrating more and focusing on one ball at a time. That approach has really helped me."There are two coaches who have helped me a lot. One is Ratan Kumar, who is currently our senior head coach. I also speak a lot with Ishank Jaggi bhaiya. He has helped me both mentally and with my batting. He was my Under-19 coach and helped me a lot during that phase. These two have played a big role in my development," he said."In my first year of Under-19 cricket, I scored around 550 runs, with most of my scores in the 70s and 80s. The following year, I wanted to focus more and convert those starts into bigger scores."Before facing a ball, I talk to myself. I remind myself to watch the ball and stay focused. That has helped me a lot. Jaggi bhai also helped me with this, especially when he was with the Under-19 team. I started concentrating more and focusing on one ball at a time. That approach has really helped me," Shikhar explained.During the Ranji Trophy camp in Chennai, Shikhar worked extensively on his batting, focusing particularly on playing close to his body, an aspect of his game he has worked relentlessly to improve."Before the season, I did a lot of batting drills. I focus on playing close to my body and working on my drives because those are the areas where I score most of my runs. I know my scoring areas, so I worked on them," the Jharkhand opener said."This season, I have concentrated on playing close to my body. I visualise myself playing within a box, keeping my shots close to my body. That has helped me a lot. As you saw in the Irani Trophy, the wicket was green. I kept reminding myself to play close to my body and avoid playing shots away from it. I think that is very important for an opener. You need to play straight because the SG ball deviates a lot, even after 10-12 overs. You have to be even more focused after that period. For the first 40 balls, my focus is on playing close to my body," he said.Shikhar, who opens in all three formats, says his preparation for each format is different."The preparation for red-ball and white-ball cricket is very different. You have to go back to your basics and make adjustments according to the format. In white-ball cricket, you need to be more proactive and play certain shots regularly.I remember a match against Uttar Pradesh at the Under-19 level. I was batting on 20 when a ball hit me on the chest. I went off the field and returned after we lost two wickets. We were chasing a target of 400 on the final day, and I scored an unbeaten 100. We fell 40 runs short when the day ended. That innings remains very special to me."Meanwhile, in red-ball cricket, you cannot play every shot in the same way. You have to work on the shots that are effective in white-ball cricket and practise them through specific drills. You need to prepare differently for each format and understand which shots are appropriate for the situation," he said.Shikhar Mohan has played some excellent knocks in the Duleep Trophy final and the Irani Trophy, but the innings closest to his heart remains the one he scored against Uttar Pradesh in the Cooch Behar Trophy."I remember a match against Uttar Pradesh at the Under-19 level. I was batting on 20 when a ball hit me on the chest. I went off the field and returned after we lost two wickets. We were chasing a target of 400 on the final day, and I scored an unbeaten 100. We fell 40 runs short when the day ended. That innings remains very special to me," he said.The youngster is already on the radar of several IPL franchises and has attended a trial with five-time champions Mumbai Indians. "It went well," he said.For now, Shikhar's focus remains on building on his impressive start and establishing himself as one of India's most consistent domestic batters. But with runs flowing and his ability to convert starts into big scores improving, the left-handed opener is beginning to make a compelling case for himself. If he maintains this form, a future push for India's Test opening slot may not be outside the realm of possibility.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Vipraj Nigam, Suryansh Shedge save India A from a whitewash against Australia A
articles.summary: PUDUCHERRY: When India ‘A’ were staring at the prospect of a whitewash, Suryansh Shedge and Vipraj Nigam demonstrated why allrounders can be invaluable
articles.body: PUDUCHERRY: When India ‘A’ were staring at the prospect of a whitewash, Suryansh Shedge and Vipraj Nigam demonstrated why allrounders can be invaluable assets. They rescued a faltering batting unit before the bowlers completed a 49-run victory over Australia ‘A’ in the third unofficial One Dayer here on Sunday. Australia ‘A’, however, won the series 2-1.Shedge, a last-minute replacement for star allrounder Hardik Pandya before the series, justified his selection with a vital 66 off 60 balls in this game, while Vipraj chipped in with a 44-balls 40. Their 85-run seventh-wicket partnership lifted India ‘A’ from a precarious 159-6 to 275, giving their bowlers a competitive total to defend.While bowling too, Nigam, who bowls leg-spin, rose to the occasion and finished with 1-47. He trapped the dangerous right-handed opener Josh Phillipe (56 off 48 balls) plumb in front of the stumps, to halt the Aussie chase.Later, on the partnership with Shedge, Nigam said: “Our plan was to spend as much time at the crease as possible, because there wasn’t much batting left below us. We knew the wicket would not behave as well later on. So, our discussion was about batting for as long as possible and adding crucial runs.”For Shedge, the innings was another opportunity to underline his abilities, having claimed four wickets in the opening game of the series. The pair showed composure and attacking intent, recognising the need to spend time at the crease with little batting left below them.“In the one-day format, scoring some quick runs becomes very crucial in matches like these. So, I just try to do that,” Nigam said.India ‘A’ had made a quick start, with Prabhsimran Singh (39) and Priyansh Arya racing to a 50-run opening stand inside seven overs. However, Scott’s short-ball strategy accounted for Prabhsimran before Devdutt Padikkal’s disappointing series continued. The lefthander finished with just three runs across three innings.Priyansh (49) fell agonisingly short of a half-century, while Rajat Patidar (3) and Nishant Sindhu (5) departed cheaply. From 83 without loss, India ‘A’ slumped to 118-5. After skipper Ruturaj Gaikwad (33), too, was dismissed, it was left to Nigam and Shedge to set up the win.Brief scores:India ‘A’ 275 all out in 47.3 overs (S Shedge 66, P Arya 49, V Nigam 40; B Dwarshuis 3-38, W Sutherland 3-44, L Scott 2-27).Australia ‘A’ 226 all out in 46.2 overs (G Singh 3-56, Y Thakur 2-35, N Sindhu 2-42). India ‘A’ won by 49 runs.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Why have India ‘A’ tours during Ranji Trophy, asks Dilip Vengsarkar
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Former India captain Dilip Vengsarkar has criticised the BCCI’s decision to send an India A team on a shadow tour of New Zealand during the
articles.body: MUMBAI: Former India captain Dilip Vengsarkar has criticised the BCCI’s decision to send an India A team on a shadow tour of New Zealand during the 2026-27 Ranji Trophy season.A 15-member India A squad, led by wicketkeeper-batter Dhruv Jurel, will tour New Zealand for three four-day matches in Lincoln and Christchurch from Oct 24 to Nov 7, ahead of India’s two-Test series there.“Why do you have an India A tour when the Ranji Trophy season is in progress? What’s the point of holding the Ranji Trophy then?” Vengsarkar told TOI.“This idea of having a shadow tour when your own domestic season is on is plain ridiculous because you are diluting the importance of your premier domestic tournament.”Most players picked for the India A tour are likely to feature in only the opening round of the Ranji Trophy before leaving for New Zealand.“If your best domestic players are playing for India A during the Ranji Trophy, then performances of those who score runs and take wickets in the Ranji Trophy get devalued,” said Vengsarkar, a former India chief selector.“It’s beyond me why these A tours are being organised during the domestic season.”Vengsarkar has previously questioned the BCCI’s scheduling of India A tours and home series during the domestic calendar.This season, the Irani Cup between 2025-26 Ranji Trophy champions Jammu & Kashmir and Rest of India also lost some sheen as IndiaA were simultaneously playing Australia A in two multi-day matches in Puducherry.The opening round of the Ranji Trophy has also clashed with the three-match one-day series between India A and Australia A.The BCCI introduced shadow tours to help fringe players get used to overseas conditions before the senior team’s assignment, ensuring ready reserves if required.Vengsarkar, however, does not agree with the logic.“If you want your players to acclimatise early to the conditions and local environment, then send your main team early,” the 116-Test veteran said.“There’s no point sending players who are not even going to play in the Test series.”Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Mohammed Shami gets the ball talking, sinks Delhi in Ranji Trophy
articles.summary: KALYANI: Delhi coach Vijay Dahiya wanted his boys to live up to the opportunity of facing ‘almost’ an Indian pace attack against Bengal, featuring
articles.body: KALYANI: Delhi coach Vijay Dahiya wanted his boys to live up to the opportunity of facing ‘almost’ an Indian pace attack against Bengal, featuring Mohammed Shami, Akash Deep and Mukesh Kumar. However, Delhi failed miserably in that exercise and were bowled out for just 240 on Day 1 of the Ranji Trophy Elite Group ‘C’ clash at the Bengal Cricket Academy ground here on Sunday.The Bengal pace trio shared seven of those 10 wickets after Bengal skipper Abhimanyu Easwaran won the toss and had no hesitations in electing to field first. Offspinner Aamir Gani was also among wickets, returning with 3 for 45. Shami led the pack picking up 4 for 30, while Akash Deep got 2 for 74 and Mukesh 1 for 43.Talks about the possibility of Shami making a comeback to the national team gained steam after veteran Bhuvneshwar Kumar was drafted into the India T20I side for the New Zealand series after a gap of four years. The 36-year-old Shami might not be fit as fiddle, he might not be delivering at 140 kph plus now, but he still remains as effective as ever.Shami joined the Bengal side only a day before the match and did not get to practice with the boys.But on Sunday, he took the new ball and made it talk. He spread his 17.3 overs across six spells on the day. “It was too hot and humid today and there’s no point bowling long spells on this wicket which was on the slower side. I planned going for three-four overs at a stretch, because you should also conserve energy and stay prepared in case a partnership happens,” Shami said of his plans at the end of day’s play.He picked up a wicket each in his second, fourth, fifth and sixth spells. Except for the fourth spell when Shami fired five overs, all his other spells were of three-overseach before he wrapped up the innings picking up Delhi’s highest scorer Hritik Shokeen (56) caught by Sudip Chatterjee in the first slip on the third delivery of his last spell. Asked about his ability to move the ball both ways, Shami said, “it’s difficult to explain. articles.summary: Maaz Sadaqat narrowly missed his maiden T20I century, but his explosive batting helped Pakistan beat Sri Lanka by 82 runs in the second T20 International
articles.body: Maaz Sadaqat narrowly missed his maiden T20I century, but his explosive batting helped Pakistan beat Sri Lanka by 82 runs in the second T20 International in Rawalpindi on Sunday. The victory gave Pakistan an unassailable 2-0 lead in the three-match series.Sadaqat smashed 96 off 51 balls, while Sahibzada Farhan scored 73 off 44 deliveries as Pakistan posted 215/3, their highest T20 total at home. Mohammad Imran then took three wickets for just 11 runs to restrict Sri Lanka to 133/7, giving Pakistan their biggest T20I win against the visitors.Sadaqat and Farhan power Pakistan to 215Pakistan made the most of Sri Lanka's poor fielding, with the visitors dropping three catches during the innings. Sadaqat, who was dropped on 44, and Farhan, who got reprieves on two and 11, made the opposition pay.The pair added 88 runs for the second wicket in just 49 balls, putting Pakistan in a strong position. Farhan hit five sixes and four fours before his innings ended in the 15th over when he was caught by Dasun Shanaka.Sadaqat continued his attack and shared another quick partnership with Hasan Nawaz, who remained unbeaten on 19. The pair added 72 runs off just 31 balls for the third wicket.Sadaqat hit seven sixes and six fours before being dismissed off the final delivery of the innings. His seven sixes matched the record for the most sixes by a Pakistan batter in a T20 match.Pakistan scored 70 runs in the final five overs to finish on 215/3. Their previous highest T20 total at home was 208/3 against the West Indies in Karachi five years ago.Imran leads Pakistan's bowling attackSri Lanka struggled to keep up with the required scoring rate during their chase and kept losing wickets at regular intervals.Medium pacer Mohammad Imran led Pakistan's bowling effort with figures of 3/11. His performance helped restrict Sri Lanka to 133/7 and seal a comfortable victory.Maheesh Theekshana remained unbeaten on 32, while Chamindu Wickramasinghe scored 29. Kamindu Mendis contributed 23 and Sineth Jayawardena made 22, but the rest of the batting order failed to build partnerships.The result gave Pakistan their biggest T20I victory against Sri Lanka in terms of runs.Farhan confident after series winPakistan captain Farhan was pleased with the team's performance and said the side was moving in the right direction."It's a good win and we are shaping up well," said Pakistan skipper Farhan."If we continue this way we will end up scoring more than 200 every time, so we will play with the same intensity."Sri Lanka captain Kusal Mendis, meanwhile, pointed to the team's fielding as a major reason for the defeat."We have done well in terms of fielding in the last few tournaments but unfortunately we have not been up to the mark and that's why we have struggled," said Mendis.The two teams will meet for the third and final T20I on Tuesday. articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India batter Tilak Varma was involved in an unusual run-out during the third T20I against West Indies on Sunday after a misunderstanding with
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India batter Tilak Varma was involved in an unusual run-out during the third T20I against West Indies on Sunday after a misunderstanding with Axar Patel cost him his wicket.The incident took place in the 17th over, with Gudakesh Motie bowling to Axar. The Indian all-rounder flicked a low full toss towards deep backward square leg, where Kamil Pooran dived to prevent the ball from reaching the boundary.How Tilak Varma got run outTilak and Axar seemed convinced that Pooran had touched the boundary rope while attempting the save. Assuming that the ball would be called a four, the two batters completed a single before exchanging a fist bump in the middle of the pitch.However, Pooran had managed to stop the ball just before it reached the boundary and quickly returned it to the field.Axar, who was facing the delivery, realised the situation and grounded his bat at the non-striker's end just in time. Tilak, meanwhile, continued walking towards his crease, unaware that the ball was still in play.Motie collected the ball and broke the stumps at the bowler's end. The third umpire reviewed the incident, first confirming that Pooran had made a clean save before ruling Tilak run out.Tilak departed after scoring 28 off 16 balls, including four fours, as India's lack of awareness led to an unusual dismissal.India recover after Tilak's dismissalDespite losing Tilak in the closing stages, India posted 223 in their 20 overs. Abhishek Sharma provided the biggest contribution with a 30-ball 69, including five sixes.Abhishek and Ishan Kishan put on 108 runs off just 40 balls. Kishan scored 37 off 18 deliveries before Roston Chase stumped him. Chase also dismissed India captain Shreyas Iyer lbw for one.The two wickets triggered a mini-collapse, with India losing four wickets for 20 runs to slip to 135/5.Arshdeep and Dhir guide India to victoryWest Indies had chased down a target of 250 in the second T20I, but India bounced back in the third match to win by 14 runs and take a 2-1 lead in the five-match series.Arshdeep Singh picked up three wickets for 44 runs, while Naman Dhir claimed two for 39 as West Indies finished on 209/7.Pooran scored 42 and Shimron Hetmyer made 43, adding 60 runs for the second wicket. Dhir dismissed both batters to put India back in control during the middle overs.Sherfane Rutherford scored 32 off 20 balls, while Shamar Springer remained unbeaten on 35 off just 11 deliveries. Springer struck three sixes in the final over against Axar Patel, but West Indies fell short of the target.After the match, India captain Shreyas Iyer praised the confidence shown by his bowlers."It was wonderful to see the bowlers being confident," India captain Shreyas Iyer said after the game. "The clarity was very much visible when I was interacting. They were ready to take up the challenge, and that's what we want."India had won the series opener by eight wickets in Lucknow before West Indies levelled the contest with a six-wicket victory in Ranchi. Sunday's win put India back in front at 2-1.The fourth T20I will be played in Hyderabad on Wednesday.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Ranji Trophy: Captain Siddhesh Lad stands tall for Mumbai against Chandigarh
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Siddhesh Lad carried last season’s rich form into the new one, playing a captain’s hand to rescue Mumbai on a testing opening day of their Elite
articles.body: MUMBAI: Siddhesh Lad carried last season’s rich form into the new one, playing a captain’s hand to rescue Mumbai on a testing opening day of their Elite Group D Ranji Trophy match against Chandigarh at the Wankhede Stadium on Sunday.Lad, Mumbai’s dependable crisis man, remained unbeaten on 80 off 176 balls, with eight fours, as the hosts reached 249/5 at stumps after being asked to bat first.The 34-year-old, who was Mumbai’s highest run-getter in the 2025-26 Ranji Trophy with 774 runs in eight matches, spent 255 minutes at the crease and completed 5,000 first-class runs for Mumbai on his first day as captain.Mumbai were in trouble at 144/4 in the 57th over after Sarfaraz Khan fell for 1 shortly before tea. Lad then added 40 for the fifth wicket with wicketkeeper-batter Akash Anand, who made 22 off 36 balls.After Anand was caught at slip off left-arm spinner Nishunk Birla, Lad found another steady partner in Shams Mulani. The pair added an unbroken 68 off 98 balls for the sixth wicket, with Mulani unbeaten on 27.Lad reached his 31st first-class half-century off 135 balls and is now closing in on his 16th first-class hundred.Mumbai were hit early when India Test opener Yashasvi Jaiswal fell for a 13-ball duck, edging Jagjit Singh to second slip in the third over. Sarfaraz was later adjudged lbw to pacer Nikhil Dhanda while shouldering arms. The decision left him visibly unhappy.Sarfaraz’s wicket came soon after Musheer Khan was caught behind off Dhanda, giving Chandigarh two key breakthroughs in successive overs. Dhanda finished the day as the pick of the bowlers with 3/44 in 15 overs. Musheer had earlier made a patient 65 off 149 balls, with four fours. He and vice-captain Ayush Mhatre rebuilt the innings after Jaiswal’s early dismissal, adding 76 for the second wicket in 145 balls. Mhatre showed more enterprise during his 48 off 82 balls, hitting seven fours and a six, before Dhanda bowled him with one that came back in. Musheer and Lad then added 65 for the third wicket.Mumbai head coach Omkar Salvi praised Lad’s commitment to red-ball cricket and his influence on younger players.“I think it’s his passion to play red-ball cricket. He is very passionate about it, which helps him and the team. The way he guides the younger players, his calmness, it enables them to express themselves,” Salvi said after the day’s play. “Over the last two seasons, the way Siddhesh has grown as a player, you can see his leadership qualities. His calm demeanour at the crease brings calmness to the dressing room. He has seen highs and lows, so he is a very settled player now. He uses his experience very well, and it helps the team.”Brief Scores: Mumbai 249 for 5 in 84 overs (Siddhesh Lad 80, Musheer Khan 65; Rohit Dhanda 3/44) vs ChandigarhStay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Ranji Trophy: Karan Lamba hits unbeaten ton as Rajasthan batters make Tamil Nadu toil on a flat deck
articles.summary: JAIPUR: Sidelined for the last couple of years despite scoring a hundred on debut, Karan Lamba relaunched himself in style with a brilliant unbeaten
articles.body: JAIPUR: Sidelined for the last couple of years despite scoring a hundred on debut, Karan Lamba relaunched himself in style with a brilliant unbeaten century to provide Rajasthan a strong start against Tamil Nadu in the Ranji Trophy opener at the Sawai Mansingh Stadium here on Sunday.Karan, who last played Ranji tie in 2024, proved a point or two to his detractors by slamming his second ton of his career as Rajasthan reached 286 for 4 on Day 1.The opening day belonged to two former U-23 teammates – Karan and debutant Rohan Rajbhar. While the latter struck an undefeated 103 (133balls, 11x4, 1x6), the former missed the hundred by a whisker by falling on 95 on his first-class debut.At stumps, vice-captain Mahipal Lomror was giving Karan company on 31 off 48 balls (5x4) as visitors toiled hard throughout the day on a placid track.For Tamil Nadu medium-pacer Saravana Kumar, it was a day to remember. The 37-year-old, who made his First-Class debut in 2022 and last played in 2025, finished the day with 3-52. With not much on offer, the paceman’s work-ethic stood out as he bowled 19 overs through the day and got one each in every session.Captaining the Rajasthan side for the first time in Ranji, Manav Suthar won the toss and did not hesitate to bat first. Rajasthan lost opener Sachin Yadav (1) quite cheaply as Saravana Kumar trapped him on the first ball of his spell.Sumit Godara joined in the second over of the day and steadied the ship with Rohan with a solid 104-run stand to deny the visitors any further advantage.At lunch Rajasthan were strongly placed 100-1. Godara, who was batting on 49 at the break, did not add anything to his score and was dismissed in the fourth over in the post-lunch session.Karan was off the mark in style and dealt mostly in boundaries. The young duo of Rohan and Karan shared a 125-run stand for the third wicket before the visitors’ 37-year-old seamer Saravana snuffed out Rohan. His short ball kissed the opener’s gloves before landing in the safe hands of wicketkeeper N Jagadeesan.Trying to clear the mid-wicket fence, Kartik Sharma threw his wicket away to Washington Sundar, giving the visitors hope.However, Karan gelled well with Mahipal to restore the home team’s advantage.Having waited since Feb 2024 for a Ranji game, Karan did not look at his knock as a fitting answer to selectors. He said he just did what he needed to.“I have to do my job. Performing is in my hands, I focus on that. I don’t fret over selection too much; for me it’s all about how I can improve my game,” said Karan.Karan, who brought up his second FC century with a backfoot square drive for four off Saravana, admitted that the flat track helped his cause. “The wicket was good to bat on. You rarely get such flat tracks, so I made sure to cash in,” he said.Besides being teammates in the U-23 team last year, Rohan and Karan have both represented Jaipur at the district level and that helped their partnership.“It helped our running between the wickets. Having played together for a long time, we don’t usually have misunderstandings,” the 21-year-old said.“You can get selected from anywhere. It’s not that they will only pick from Ranji Trophy. If you perform well at the U-23s, they have their eyes on you anyway,” added Karan.Though Sunday’s ton came after two years of wait, Karan enjoyed his century on Ranji debut in 2023 against Jharkhand in Jaipur more. “As a cricketer, it is a dream to play in the Ranji Trophy. The day I realised that dream I hit a hundred so that was more satisfying,” he said.Sai Sudharsan joins TN squadCatching everybody by surprise, Sai Sudharsan joins the TN squad to boost the batting line-up.“Sai came at 10pm on Saturday night from Puducherry. We didn't know about his arrival until he landed at the hotel,” said TN team manager Goutham Dangi.Brief Scores: Rajasthan 286/4 in 85 overs (Karan Lamba 103*, Rohan Rajbhar 95, Sumit Godara 49, Mahipal Lomror 31*; Saravana Kumar 3-52, Washington Sundar 1-49).Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: Bihar cricket is poised to take a significant step forward when the newly built Rajgir International Cricket Stadium hosts its first-ever BCCI domestic fixture, with Bihar facing Uttar Pradesh in their Ranji Trophy Elite Group A opener beginning on Sunday.More than just the start of Bihar’s 2026-27 domestic season, the match marks the official arrival of Rajgir on India’s first-class cricket map. The emergence of a modern international-standard venue in Rajgir is being viewed as a major boost to the state’s long-term cricketing ambitions. Officials believe the stadium can play a crucial role in attracting more domestic fixtures, providing better facilities to local players and strengthening Bihar’s cricket ecosystem.The fixture has generated considerable excitement among fans, who will have the opportunity to witness top-level domestic cricket at a venue that could become a centrepiece of Bihar’s sporting development in the coming years.Adding to the occasion is the arrival of a star-studded Uttar Pradesh side. The visitors landed in Gaya ahead of the fixture on Thursday and were welcomed by Bihar Cricket Association (BCA) officials. The UP squad features several prominent domestic and IPL players, including Rinku Singh, Yash Dayal, Aryan Juyal and Prashant Veer.While the presence of established names is expected to draw spectators, the larger significance of the match lies in what it represents for Bihar cricket. The state’s new domestic season will begin on a fresh stage, one built with the aim of matching the standards of leading cricket centres across the country.Bihar Cricket Association has made extensive arrangements for the match and is hopeful that a successful hosting of the fixture will pave the way for more BCCI tournaments at the venue in the future.So, the first ball on Sunday morning, it would be a victory for Bihar cricket with the unveiling of a modern cricketing landmark that has the potential to transform the state’s sporting landscape and place Rajgir firmly on India’s domestic cricket circuit.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Remain ruthless': Abhishek Sharma reveals Team India's huddle talk during West Indies thriller
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Team India did not want to give West Indies any chance to fight back in the third T20I in Indore.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Team India did not want to give West Indies any chance to fight back in the third T20I in Indore. Abhishek Sharma revealed that the team discussed staying ruthless in the huddle as the hosts defended their total in Indore on Sunday.India secured a 14-run victory to take a 2-1 lead in the five-match series. After scoring 223, the hosts restricted West Indies to 209/7, with Arshdeep Singh taking three wickets and Naman Dhir claiming two.However, West Indies kept the pressure on India until the final over. Shamar Springer smashed an unbeaten 35 off just 11 balls, including three sixes and a boundary, but could not take his team over the line.Abhishek, who led India's batting with 69 off 30 deliveries, spoke about the team's approach during the post-match press conference.Abhishek reveals what India discussed in the huddleAbhishek said India knew West Indies had the ability to turn a match around quickly. The team had witnessed this in the previous game and wanted to avoid giving the visitors another opportunity to stage a comeback.“I think the West Indies is the kind of team against whom you can never say that the match has swung completely in our favor. That was in our minds, because we saw in the last match as well that whichever batter walks in, given the conditions here, it's very easy for them to take the game away from anywhere. So that was in our minds; even when wickets were falling, the talk in the huddle was that we need to remain ruthless from here on, not let them off the hook, and not give them even a single chance to make a comeback,” he said.Springer's attack keeps India on their toesSpringer's late hitting showed why India were determined to stay focused rather than assume the match was already won.Springer made India's task difficult with his aggressive batting towards the end of the chase. Abhishek admitted he was surprised by some of the shots the West Indies batter played and stressed the importance of executing plans under pressure.“If you saw today, the way Springer batted, I got really surprised by the way he played those shots; they weren't easy shots. In that case, you have to be on your toes all the time. Even if they are 50 for 5, they have the capability to turn things around. We were very much prepared this time that we had to be ruthless. Even if we had a good powerplay with the ball, we couldn't afford to give them even one bad ball. We just wanted to execute our plans, and that's what we did,” he said.India's bowlers managed to defend the total despite Springer's late assault. The victory put the hosts ahead in the series, with the fourth T20I scheduled to take place in Hyderabad on Wednesday.Abhishek surpasses Suryakumar Yadav's recordAbhishek also achieved a significant milestone during his innings in Indore. He became the fastest batter to score 2,000 runs in men's T20I cricket in terms of balls faced, reaching the mark in 1,024 deliveries.He broke the previous record held by former India T20I captain Suryakumar Yadav, who had taken 1,164 balls to reach 2,000 runs. Former Australia captain Aaron Finch is third on the list, having needed 1,283 deliveries.Abhishek's record-breaking effort helped India put up a challenging total and eventually secure an important win in the five-match series.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Australia v South Africa: Bad light thwarts Durban Test despite ICC changes
articles.summary: More than 60 overs have been lost from the first Test between South Africa and Australia despite a change by the ICC. Has cricket missed a trick?
articles.body:
It is one of cricket's oldest and most frustrating problems: bad light.

A fascinating passage of play halted when things get too gloomy.

The issue has reared its head again this week in the fascinating first Test between South Africa and Australia in Durban, wiping out more than 60 overs across the first three days.

The fact a solution was added to cricket's rules just last week, an option so far unused around the world, only adds to the frustration.

Australia veterans shine against South Africa

Play is already starting early, at 09:30 local time in Durban, given this is the first October Test at Kingsmead, a setting where the sun sets shortly after 18:00 at this time of year on South Africa's eastern coast.

Still, on day one, play was halted at 15:23 local time after clouds built. Only 65.2 of the scheduled 90 overs had been bowled and the players were unable to return.

Day two was slightly better with play continuing until 16:25, but that finish was still 35 minutes earlier than it could have been. Day three's end came at 16:31.

On each occasion, the first two sessions have been played in hot, sunny conditions, only for clouds to build in the afternoon - a familiar weather pattern in Durban.

"Very quickly in the morning, as temperatures have risen inland as the sun heats the ground, a sea breeze has formed with winds coming from the sea into Durban," said BBC weather presenter Chris Fawkes.

"This has increased humidity levels through the morning and brought some cloud in. As temperatures have started to fall again towards the evening, this has increased the relative humidity with the air getting increasingly saturated.

"That has caused the cloud to get thicker and lower."

What about the change in playing conditions?

Following a trial earlier in the year , the International Cricket Council amended its playing conditions to allow the pink ball to be used in Tests.

It was supposed to help in these exact scenarios.

Crucially, it does not allow a red ball to be switched for pink when the light becomes poor - something previously suggested by former England captain Michael Vaughan .

Instead, if problems with the light are expected, it allows teams to agree before a Test starts to use the pink ball throughout.

No such discussions were held between the Proteas and Australia before the Durban Test, however.

'There is a stigma around the pink ball'

The pink ball has been a fixture of day-night Tests because it is easier to see than the darker red in night-time conditions.

Former South Africa bowler Shaun Pollock was part of the ICC committee which recommended the change and he believes there is a "stigma" around the pink ball in the game.

"They say it moves too much," Pollock said.

"If Australia were 124-6 [as they were on day one] and we were using the pink ball, everyone would have said it was the pink ball's fault.

"If Australia were 124-6 and got to 390 [as they did in their first innings] everyone in South Africa would have said it was the pink ball's fault, that it got soft.

"The pink ball would have meant we played 45 more overs of Test cricket and that is why I am keen to introduce it, and not just for day-night games."

Why might teams not want to use the pink ball?

One narrative exists that the pink ball moves more under floodlights, though that is not backed up by ball tracking data.

Instead, various batters have spoken about the pink ball being more difficult to see. Batting averages are lowest in the evening of day-night matches.

Australia have also played in 15 of Test cricket's day-nighters - 10 more than anyone else.

Unsurprisingly, the four leading wicket-takers in day-night matches are all Australians. Left-armer Mitchell Starc's haul of 89 wickets in 15 Tests has positioned him as the undisputed pink-ball king.

You would not blame teams if they would rather face Australia with the red ball.

Former South Africa bowler Vernon Philander said he prefers the idea of switching balls during the match if conditions require it, but that would raise questions over the Test's integrity.

Is the potential injustice of one team having to face a pink ball outweighed by the need to get more action of the field?

"They have to take it out of the hands of the players completed and enforce it from the umpires' point of view that the pink ball will become in play when the light has faded enough," Philander said.

"You are always going to have the argument of who is ahead of the game.

"I would like to see the ICC enforce it on to the officials to make that call."

articles.title: India vs West Indies: ‘Plan B’ against Abhishek Sharma revealed! India star says he knew West Indies’ strategy
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India opener Abhishek Sharma knew the West Indies had a plan to contain him. His response was simple: play better than their plan.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India opener Abhishek Sharma knew the West Indies had a plan to contain him. His response was simple: play better than their plan.The left-hander’s explosive 30-ball 69 proved decisive as India defeated the West Indies by 14 runs in the third T20I to take a 2-1 lead in the five-match series. West Indies all-rounder Shamar Springer later revealed that the visitors’ Plan B against the in-form opener was to adopt a defensive approach and restrict him to singles and twos rather than allow him to continue his big-hitting spree.Abhishek smashed six fours and five sixes, recording his 14th T20I half-century and becoming the fastest player to reach 2,000 runs in the format in terms of balls faced. His 108-run partnership with Ishan Kishan, who scored 37, helped India post 223 before the bowlers held their nerve to restrict the visitors to 209/7.Springer reveals West Indies’ Plan BWith Abhishek initially taking on Roston Chase’s off-spin, the West Indies had to reconsider their approach against the dangerous opener. Springer explained that the team decided to focus on damage control rather than attempt an aggressive dismissal.“He is a world-class player. Kudos to him, for sure. But I guess our plan B is to just be as defensive as possible and try to make him get singles and twos, running at moments. Nothing too extravagant,” Springer told reporters after the match.“It was just a matter of trying to pull him back and be as impressive as possible. Because there's not much control you can really have here. The wickets are so good and those players are world-class players and they're the best for a reason. So, it's not really much you can really do besides be defensive,” he added.The strategy, however, could not prevent Abhishek from giving India a flying start. The opener’s assault provided the home side with the cushion they needed to withstand a late West Indies charge.Springer himself threatened to turn the contest around with an unbeaten 35 off just 11 balls, including four sixes and two fours, but the visitors eventually fell 14 runs short.‘I had to play better than that’: AbhishekAbhishek acknowledged that the West Indies’ tactics against him were on his mind, particularly when Chase opened the bowling and the field was set to challenge his preferred scoring areas.“I wouldn't say it was deliberate, but it was there in my mind that they had a plan against me,” Abhishek said.“(With the) off-spinner bowling against me, it was just a battle between him and me. I gave him respect in the first over because he is bowling really well in this series, so it is just the plan that went pretty well for me as well.”The opener, however, insisted that his strokeplay was dictated by the field rather than any premeditated attempt to target a particular area.“...because in the powerplay, I was trying to just get a few runs and they had a plan for me, and I had to play better than that,” he said. “I don't think and play deliberately. It just happens when I see the field placement, whenever they have a field placement which allows me to just give myself room and play those shots.”India stay ruthless despite late scareAbhishek said India were determined not to let the West Indies back into the contest, knowing the visitors possessed enough batting firepower to threaten even in difficult situations.“West Indies is such a team that you can never say that the match is now on our side,” he said, recalling how the opposition’s batters had shown their ability to change the course of a game.“That was in our mind because we saw in the last match that whichever batsman comes in, (with) the conditions that we have here, it is very easy for them to take the match to their side.”“So that was in our mind even when we were losing wickets, we were saying that we would be ruthless thereon and we will not give them a single chance to come back,” Abhishek added.Springer felt the West Indies could have taken the chase closer, pointing to missed scoring opportunities and the pitch playing lower than expected. He also credited the Indian bowlers for using the conditions effectively.India’s 14-run victory gave them a 2-1 series lead, with Abhishek’s early onslaught once again underlining why opposition sides are searching for ways to contain him.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Record alert! Tilak Varma joins elite fielding club with India's best catch ratio in T20Is
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India vice-captain Tilak Varma may have endured an unusual run-out in the third T20I against West Indies, but the match also brought a
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India vice-captain Tilak Varma may have endured an unusual run-out in the third T20I against West Indies, but the match also brought a significant personal milestone for the left-handed batter. Tilak became only the fifth Indian fielder to complete 50 catches in T20Is during Sunday's match in Indore, joining an elite list featuring Rohit Sharma, Hardik Pandya, Suryakumar Yadav and Virat Kohli.What makes Tilak's achievement particularly impressive is the efficiency with which he has reached the landmark. His 50 catches have come in just 68 T20I appearances, giving him a dismissals-per-innings ratio of 0.757 — the best among Indian fielders with at least 50 outfield catches in the format.Globally, Tilak's ratio is second only to the United Arab Emirates' Muhammad Waseem, who has taken 76 catches in 99 outings at a ratio of 0.767. Among the 34 players to have taken at least 50 outfield catches in men's T20Is, only Waseem has a better ratio.Tilak joins India's elite catching clubTilak's achievement places him alongside some of India's most accomplished fielders in the shortest format. Rohit leads the list with 65 catches, followed by Hardik with 64, Suryakumar with 58 and Kohli with 54.Most catches as a fielder for India in T20IsRohit Sharma — 65Hardik Pandya — 64Suryakumar Yadav — 58Virat Kohli — 54Tilak Varma — 50Reaching the milestone in just 68 appearances underlines Tilak's contribution in the field, with his catches-per-innings record placing him among the most efficient outfielders in men's T20I cricket.Bizarre run-out mars Tilak's outingThe milestone came during a match in which Tilak was also involved in an unusual dismissal. Batting in the 17th over, he and Axar Patel appeared to believe that West Indies fielder Kamil Pooran had touched the boundary rope while stopping a shot off Gudakesh Motie.The pair completed a single and exchanged a fist bump, assuming the ball would be called a four. But Pooran had kept the ball in play and returned it quickly. Axar made his ground at the striker's end, while Tilak continued towards his crease, seemingly unaware of the situation. Motie collected the ball and broke the stumps at the bowler's end, with the third umpire confirming the run-out.Tilak departed for 28 off 16 balls, including four boundaries. India, however, recovered to post 223, powered by Abhishek Sharma's 69 off 30 balls, and went on to beat West Indies by 14 runs.Arshdeep Singh claimed three wickets and Naman Dhir took two as West Indies finished on 209/7. The victory gave India a 2-1 lead in the five-match series.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: How watching Virat Kohli's videos helped Australia A star tackle Indian spinners
articles.summary: Nathan McSweeney used YouTube videos of Virat Kohli and Steve Smith to prepare for the challenge of batting against spin in India.
articles.body: Nathan McSweeney used YouTube videos of Virat Kohli and Steve Smith to prepare for the challenge of batting against spin in India. His preparation proved effective as the Australia A batter topped the run charts in the one-day series against India A, helping his team secure a 2-1 win in Puducherry.McSweeney scored 194 runs in three innings at an average of 64.66 and a strike rate of 83.62. His consistent performances also earned him the Player of the Series award.McSweeney reveals how he prepared for Indian conditionsMcSweeney explained that studying how top batters handle spin was an important part of his preparation for the tour. He also relied on analysis and data shared by the team's support staff."I think obviously coming to India as, an Australian, it's a heavy spin focus and you try and work hard and watch the great Indian players on how they play spin," McSweeney told the host broadcaster after the white-ball series ended on Sunday."[Watching] Virat Kohli on YouTube trying to study how he goes about it, Steve Smith, other Australians that have come over and done really well. So, there's plenty of analysts and data that we are given as well. So, it's nice to action that out in the middle and execute it fairly well."The batter put his preparation to good use against India's spinners. He used his feet effectively, played sweeps and stepped out of his crease to disrupt the bowlers' plans. His ability to play the ball softly into gaps also helped him score consistently on challenging surfaces.Australia A win one-day series 2-1Australia A started the series with a 125-run victory. After scoring 274, they bowled India A out for 149.The visitors then won the second match by 69 runs, scoring 275 before restricting India A to 206.India A prevented Australia A from completing a clean sweep by winning the third match by 49 runs. India A posted 275 and dismissed Australia A for 226.Australia A nevertheless took the series 2-1, with McSweeney's batting proving crucial to their success.Reflecting on the achievement, McSweeney said winning a series in India was a special result for the visiting side."I'm very pleased to come over here in good conditions and spend some time in the middle, which is always nice and a series win in India is no easy feat by any international team coming over," McSweeney said. "It's a very tough place to come and play cricket against tough competition always. So, yeah, well done to our boys and it's nice to get a series win."McSweeney wants to improve in long-format cricketBefore the one-day series, McSweeney had found it difficult to convert his starts into big scores in the unofficial Test series. Australia A lost that series 0-1, and the batter said he wanted to learn from those performances."I think I missed out in the first innings of a couple of those games," McSweeney said. "We saw anyone that watched the four-day stuff, as the game went on it got really hard to bat. So, I think I got a couple of thirties in the second innings of both those games."But, I think where it counts, especially playing cricket in India, is in that first innings of long-form cricket if you can make a big score there. Not only is it probably easier for batting but also sets up your team to win the game. So, coming back here hopefully I get another opportunity. I'll be really trying to focus on that."Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: The Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) has shifted ongoing President’s Trophy Grade 1 matches away from Peshawar and Abbottabad following the federal
articles.body: The Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) has shifted ongoing President’s Trophy Grade 1 matches away from Peshawar and Abbottabad following the federal government’s announcement of a state of emergency and the imposition of governor’s rule in the politically troubled province of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.The venue changes come amid escalating political tensions involving the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI), the party of former prime minister Imran Khan, which had been governing the province. According to a Cricinfo report, the PCB has moved fixtures originally scheduled at Imran Khan Stadium in Peshawar and Abbottabad Cricket Stadium to venues in Sheikhupura and Lahore.The decision has disrupted the schedule as the first-class competition approaches the end of its league stage. Matches in Islamabad and Rawalpindi, the other two host cities, will continue as planned.PCB revises venues as political tensions escalateThe emergency was announced following presidential approval of recommendations submitted by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif’s federal cabinet. The political developments also led to the detention of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi and some members of his cabinet, according to Pakistan’s junior interior minister Talal Chaudhry, who confirmed the detentions to Reuters.Under the revised schedule, Ghani will face Hyderabad Kingsmen Academy at Rana Naveed Academy in Sheikhupura from October 14. The match between Sui Northern Gas Pipelines Limited (SNGPL) and Oil and Gas Development Company Limited (OGDCL) has been moved to the LCCA Ground in Lahore, adjacent to Gaddafi Stadium, with the fixture also beginning on October 14.The current round is the penultimate one of the league stage, with the sixth round beginning on Monday. articles.body: NEW DELHI: India’s Naman Dhir is making an impact with the ball despite being primarily a batting all-rounder, and the 26-year-old believes his ability to read a batter’s intentions is helping him deliver crucial breakthroughs in T20Is.Dhir claimed two wickets (2/39) in India’s 14-run victory over the West Indies in the third T20I at the Holkar Stadium in Indore on Sunday, helping the hosts take a 2-1 lead in the five-match series. The off-spinner dismissed Shimron Hetmyer and Kamil Pooran during the visitors’ chase of 224, adding to the three wickets (3/31) he took on his T20I debut during the West Indies series.Explaining his approach, Dhir said his bowling relies on disciplined lines and lengths, variations in pace and an understanding of the batter’s technique.“As an off-spinner, I don’t have too many variations, so I have to rely on my line and length and vary my pace. That has always been my thinking. As they say that in T20 cricket, an attacking option can also be a defensive option because there is nothing better than taking a wicket,” Dhir told JioStar.“It helps being a batter because you understand the batter’s stance, where his backlift is coming from, his guard and the kind of shots he can play. I keep observing these things when I bowl,” he added.‘He was looking to play every shot towards the leg side’Dhir offered an insight into how he planned the dismissal of Pooran, explaining that he had identified the batter’s preferred scoring areas and wanted to restrict his room to play freely.“I didn’t plan to concede three sixes and then take a wicket. For instance, when Kamil Pooran was batting, he was looking to play every shot towards the leg side and get room to free his arms, so I wanted to cramp him for room,” he said.“I made a couple of errors in the first two deliveries. I knew I was bowling my third over, the batter was set, and with the run rate being high, he was bound to take a chance. And, ultimately, he got out playing exactly the kind of shot I wanted him to, getting caught at square-leg.”“So, these little things help me a lot, and as a bowler, I keep looking for such small details,” Dhir added.Batting remains Dhir’s primary roleDespite his growing contributions with the ball, Dhir made it clear that batting remains his primary responsibility in the Indian setup. He said the team management expects him to provide flexibility in the lower middle order while delivering two or three overs when required.“I am a batting all-rounder. I got an opportunity to bat in this game, but I am a bit disappointed that I couldn’t capitalise on it,” he said.Dhir added that the Impact Player rule in the IPL had reduced his bowling opportunities, but stressed that bowling had always been part of his game.“With the ball, my responsibility is to bowl two or three overs economically whenever the team needs me,” he said.The all-rounder is not looking too far ahead despite his promising start to international cricket.“I don’t function that way, by looking too far ahead. articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India’s bowlers had a clear plan to stop Shai Hope’s impressive run against them, and left-arm pacer Arshdeep Singh was delighted to see it
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India’s bowlers had a clear plan to stop Shai Hope’s impressive run against them, and left-arm pacer Arshdeep Singh was delighted to see it work in the third T20I against the West Indies in Indore on Sunday.Hope had been in sensational form across the ODI and T20I series, scoring back-to-back centuries in the 50-over format before producing a half-century in the opening T20I and an unbeaten 102 in the second. But the West Indies captain managed just five runs in Indore, bowled by Arshdeep in the second over as India restricted the visitors to 209/7 while defending 223.India won by 14 runs to take a 2-1 lead in the five-match series, with Arshdeep finishing with three wickets, including the crucial dismissals of Hope, Sherfane Rutherford and Keemo Paul.“Before the match, we had planned how to keep things tight to him and when you execute that plan in the match, it feels good when you get the result. I am grateful to the coaches for working through the plan and they told me that I can use this in the match and that thing got executed,” Arshdeep said in a video posted on bcci.tv on Monday.‘All six bowlers chipped in’Arshdeep credited the entire bowling attack for maintaining pressure while defending a formidable total, pointing to the collective effort that helped India bounce back after West Indies chased down 250 in the previous match.“I bowled very well. Mayank kept the pressure from the other end and all the six bowlers, all chipped in and bowled very well. It feels good when you get a little pressure for executing plans. So, it's good fun,” he said.Arshdeep also had a light-hearted moment when he apologised to Axar Patel for the mid-pitch mix-up that resulted in the all-rounder's run-out.“I would like to apologise to Axar bhai. Sorry, Axar bhai. I got you run out,” he said.The pacer said he continues to work on his batting, too, as India look for useful contributions from the lower order.“I keep trying in batting. The results are rare. But today, it just connected well. As much as the coaches trust us, we have to do it in batting as well and get a few runs down the order. So it is important to work like this in batting,” he added.Ian Bishop praises India's bowling plansFormer West Indies pacer Ian Bishop also credited India’s execution, highlighting their use of yorkers and wide lines, Arshdeep’s leadership of the attack and Naman Dhir’s support. He also pointed to the absence of dew as a factor that helped the bowlers."First of all, congratulations to India. The West Indies found a little bit of range with the ball after about over number eight through Roston Chase, then Springer, then Motie, but those runs at the back end by Prince Yadav proved crucial. Then we saw the yorkers. Shreyas Iyer mentioned at the toss that he brought Prince Yadav back into the team for the first time in the series so they could get guys bowling those yorkers and wide lines, and those are critical plans."Arshdeep is the leader of the attack, and he sussed things out quite quickly, with a little bit of help from Naman Dhir. A critical factor, obviously, was that there was no dew formation. All in all, it’s good to see the bowlers having a better day in a batsman-dominated series so far. The West Indies will look to do a few things better next time, but take nothing away from India; they deserved this win from a bowling perspective,” Bishop told JioStar.Arshdeep, meanwhile, said the relaxed atmosphere in the Indian dressing room and his willingness to learn continue to help him improve.“In the dressing room, the environment is very chill. There is no one who behaves as if they have played more or less matches. The atmosphere is very chill,” he said.“I keep trying to learn about something and get in a different skill set.
